question: The Faraizi Movement was a religious reform movement of the 19th century in _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Faraizi Movement** was a **religious reform movement** that originated in the **19th century** in the region of **Bengal**. It was initiated to bring about reforms in the practice of Islam.
 
• The movement was founded by **Haji Shariatullah**, a prominent Islamic reformer who sought to purify Islamic practices and remove corrupt practices that had crept into the religion.
 
• The term "**Faraizi**" is derived from the Arabic word "**Fard**", which refers to religious obligations. The movement emphasized the importance of adhering strictly to Islamic obligations and eliminating un-Islamic practices. *Hence, the movement originated in Bengal.*
 
• One of the key objectives of the movement was to combat the influence of **British colonial rule** and the exploitation of peasants in Bengal. The Faraizi leaders fought for the rights of the peasantry, particularly against oppressive landlords.
 
• The movement also worked to revive the **spiritual and moral integrity** of Muslims by promoting equality and unity among the community. *Hence, the movement focused on Bengal's socio-religious context.*
 
• The Faraizi Movement had a significant impact in Bengal as it sought to protect the rights of the oppressed and promote Islamic values. It also fostered a spirit of resistance against colonial oppression and socio-economic exploitation.
 
• The movement later gained momentum under the leadership of **Dudu Miyan**, the son of Haji Shariatullah, who continued the struggle for social justice and religious reform. *Hence, the movement became a major force in Bengal.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Bengal.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Haji Shariatullah:**

 
 
• **Haji Shariatullah** was the founder of the Faraizi Movement. Born in Bengal in **1781**, he traveled to Mecca for pilgrimage and returned inspired to initiate reforms in Islamic practices.
 
• He emphasized the importance of following the **Quran** and **Sunnah**, rejecting practices that were not in accordance with Islamic teachings. His efforts were aimed at purifying Islam and promoting religious obligations.
 
 
 
• **Socio-economic Impact:**
 
 
• The movement addressed the exploitation of peasants by **zamindars** (landlords) in Bengal. It fought against the oppressive **indigo plantations** and taxes imposed by the colonial government.
 
• The Faraizi leaders advocated for **social justice** and the rights of the poor, which made the movement highly popular among the peasantry.
 
• **Example:** The movement resisted the collection of taxes that were deemed un-Islamic and supported the peasants in their struggle against exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Dudu Miyan:**
 
 
• He was the son of Haji Shariatullah and took over the leadership of the movement after his father’s death. His efforts further strengthened the movement.
 
• Under his leadership, the Faraizi Movement expanded its influence and became a significant force in Bengal, advocating for both religious and social reforms.
 
• He was particularly effective in mobilizing peasants and organizing them to resist exploitation by landlords and colonial officials.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Faraizi Movement:**

 
 
• The movement played a crucial role in **reviving Islamic values** and fostering a sense of unity among Muslims in Bengal.
 
• It highlighted the importance of adhering to religious obligations and rejecting practices that contradicted Islamic teachings.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Society:**
 
 
• The movement helped empower the peasantry and resist socio-economic exploitation, contributing to the overall reform of society in Bengal.
 
• It laid the foundation for future movements that sought to address the challenges faced by the oppressed and promote social justice.
